opex.text: Liquidity management is required to ensure that adequate funds will be available to meet anticipated and unanticipated deposit withdrawals, debt service payments, investment commitments, commercial and consumer loan demand, and ongoing operating expenses. Funding sources include principal repayments on loans, sale of assets, growth in time and core deposits, short and long-term borrowings, investment securities coming due, loan prepayments and repurchase agreements. Regular loan payments are a dependable source of funds, while the sale of investment securities, deposit growth and loan prepayments are significantly influenced by general economic conditions and the level of interest rates.

prov.text: Net Interest Income: Net interest income before provision for credit losses increased by $3.76 million, or 38.1 percent, to $13.63 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $9.86 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net interest income before provision for credit losses increased by $18.91 million, or 96.5 percent, to $38.50 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $19.59 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

nonint.text: Noninterest Expense for the Three Months Ended: Noninterest expenses decreased by $2.76 million or 25.4 percent, from $10.89 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, to $8.12 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The decrease was primarily due to the $3.87 million of merger expenses recognized for the three months ended September 30, 2025 for which there was no comparable expense in 2026. The decrease was offset by a $127 thousand increase in salaries and employee benefit expenses, an increase in amortization of core deposit intangible of $178 thousand, a $144 thousand increase in net occupancy and equipment expense and a $410 thousand increase in data processing fees.

nonop.text: Interest Expense: Interest expense increased by $267 thousand or 5.9 percent to $4.82 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $4.56 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Interest expense increased by $4.74 million or 47.7 percent to $14.67 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $9.94 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in interest expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 when compared to the same periods of 2025 is primarily due to an increase in expense on deposits due to higher balances and a rising rate environment and the merger with NUBC.

pretax.text: Net Interest Income: Net interest income before provision for credit losses increased by $3.76 million, or 38.1 percent, to $13.63 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $9.86 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net interest income before provision for credit losses increased by $18.91 million, or 96.5 percent, to $38.50 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $19.59 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

tax.text: Provision for Income Taxes: The Company recorded an income tax provision of $1.13 million in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $1.02 million, or 974.3 percent, compared to $105 thousand in the third quarter of 2025. The Company recorded income tax provision of $3.35 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $2.42 million, or 259.5 percent, compared to $932 thousand for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in income tax provision for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 when compared to the same periods in 2025 is due to non-taxable income and nondeductible merger expenses recorded in the third quarter of 2025. Included in non-interest income for 2025 is the bargain purchase gain of $17.83 million, which is non-taxable as result of the tax-free exchange associated with the merger with NUBC. The Company's effective tax rate increased to 17.1% and 17.7% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 0.8% and 5.1% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.text: Net Interest Income: Net interest income before provision for credit losses increased by $3.76 million, or 38.1 percent, to $13.63 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $9.86 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net interest income before provision for credit losses increased by $18.91 million, or 96.5 percent, to $38.50 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $19.59 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest Income for the Three Months Ended: Noninterest income decreased by $17.31 million, or 91.0%, to $1.72 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from the $19.03 million recognized during the same period of 2025. Service charges on deposit accounts increased by $101 thousand to $326 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $225 thousand recognized during the same period of 2025. ATM fees and debit card income increased by $99 thousand and trust fee income increased by $262 thousand to $386 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $124 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the three months ended September 30, 2025 a bargain purchase gain of $17.83 million was recognized in association with the merger with NUBC. Net marketable equity security gains decreased by $54 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from the $60 thousand gain recognized during the same period of 2025 due to a decrease in market value in the third quarter of 2026.

intro.text: On September 24, 2024, as amended on December 4, 2024, Mifflinburg Bancorp, Inc. (“Mifflinburg”) and Northumberland Bancorp (“NUBC”) jointly announced the signing of a definitive merger agreement to combine the two companies in a strategic merger of equals. Effective August 1, 2025, the merger was completed. Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, (i) Northumberland merged with and into Mifflinburg, with Mifflinburg being the surviving entity, and (ii) The Northumberland National Bank merged with and into Mifflinburg’s wholly-owned banking subsidiary, Mifflinburg Bank & Trust Company (“Mifflinburg Bank”), with Mifflinburg Bank being the surviving bank (the “Mergers”). In connection with the Mergers, Mifflinburg changed its name to Steele Bancorp, Inc.
